verses.1: And while they were speaking to the people, the priests, the leader of the temple, and the Sadducees raised them up against the people.
verses.2: They scolded them because they were teaching the people about Jesus and telling them about the resurrection from the dead.
verses.3: And they laid their hands on them, and they were placed in a place of rest, on that day, since it was already evening.
verses.4: Many of those who listened believed his words. Thus, the number of men became thousands and five.
verses.5: On that day, their rulers, elders, and officials were gathered together in Jerusalem.
verses.6: And the high priests, including Hanna, Kaifas, Giovanni, Alexander, and all those who were of priestly origin.
verses.7: And when they were placed in the middle, they stood there. With what power or by what name did you do this?
verses.8: Then Peter, having received the Holy Spirit, said to them: “As leaders of the people and elders,
verses.9: If we were to now judge people based on their kindness toward the weak, then in which one of these situations would he be considered kind?
verses.10: It is known to all of you, and to the entire people of Israel, that in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom you crucified, and whom God raised from the dead, he appeared before you as a healthy man.
verses.11: This is the stone that comes from afar, among you, from those builders. It becomes a kind of “head” or “ornament” for the structure.
verses.12: And there is no other salvation anywhere else. For it has a different name from that given by heaven, which is what we need to find in order to be saved.
verses.13: Seeing the obedience of Peter and John, and understanding that they were people who had special abilities, they were amazed. They also realized that they were with Jesus.
verses.14: When they saw that man with them, they had nothing to say in opposition to his treatment.
verses.15: They then asked them to leave the room and go away from each other.
verses.16: Saying, “What shall we do to these people?” For indeed, it became a clear sign for all those who live in Jerusalem. We cannot deny this.
verses.17: But in order that it not spread too widely among the people, we warned them not to speak anymore about this name. No one should mention it anymore.
verses.18: And when they were called upon, they were instructed not to touch or teach in the name of Jesus at all.
verses.19: But Peter and John replied to them, “If it is right in your eyes to judge others more harshly than God does, then do so yourselves.”
verses.20: For we cannot speak what we have seen and heard, nor can we speak rightly.
verses.21: But those who were threatening them dismissed them, not finding any reason to punish them on account of the people’s actions. After all, everyone recognized the god for what he was.
verses.22: For that man was one of forty-six people who had this mark of madness.
verses.23: After that, they went before their own leaders and reported everything that the high priests and the elders had said to them.
verses.24: And those who heard this praised God with a loud voice. They said, “Lord, you who created the heavens, the earth, the sea, and all that is in them.”
verses.25: “Your son, David, who was born through the spirit of the holy father, said: ‘How can nations and peoples be destroyed and left empty?’”
verses.26: The kings of the land and their rulers gathered together in accordance with the will of the Lord and His Son.
verses.27: For they truly gathered in this city to worship your holy son Jesus, whom you have given me. There were also Herodes and Pontius Pilate, along with the people of Israel.
verses.28: Do whatever your hand and heart desire to happen.
verses.29: And also, my lord, let them be subjected to their own threats. And let your servants speak your words with complete obedience.
verses.30: In your hand, it will extend itself into signs and wonders, because of the name of your holy child Jesus.
verses.31: And when they were asked to do so, the place where they were gathered was evacuated. All of them were filled with the Holy Spirit’s power. They began to speak the words of God with great devotion.
verses.32: But the hearts and souls of all those who believed were one and the same. None of them considered anything that happened to them to be unique or special; everything was common to them all.
verses.33: And with great power, the apostles of the Lord’s resurrection gave this testimony. Their efforts were greatly beneficial to everyone.
verses.34: For none of them had any desire to do so either. After all, those who were owners of fields or houses, when they sold their possessions, did so at a high price.
verses.35: And they also stand near the feet of the apostles. Each of them was given something useful to give away.
verses.36: Joseph, who was called Barnabas by the apostles, was actually a son of deception. He was a Levite of Cyprian origin.
verses.37: He sold the land he owned, took the payment, and left it at the feet of the messengers.
